scope: Prior optical work on Gaussian packets near the inflection point of a cosine lattice band; zero quadratic diffraction, two-dimensional one-axis versus two-axis suppression, and residual cubic propagation.
method: Bounded English-language topic search with exact-title and reference chasing. Discovery used web search; scientific assessment used author-hosted PDFs, arXiv full text and original APS records. No completeness or novelty certificate is claimed.
queries: waveguide arrays zero diffraction pi/2 third order diffraction Gaussian Eisenberg 2000
discrete diffraction management zero diffraction waveguide array third order diffraction
Airy Gaussian wave packet tight binding lattice inflection point cubic dispersion
"Relativistic motion of an Airy wave packet in a lattice potential"
"Anomalous refraction and diffraction in discrete optical systems"
deduplication: DOI is the primary identity. arXiv:1001.0997 is the author version of Longhi's 2009 article, not a second paper.

records.title: The peculiarities of discrete diffraction in two-dimensional optical waveguide arrays
records.read_scope: All four PDF pages; Fig. 3 rendered and visually inspected.
located_evidence: PDF p.2, Eqs. (1)-(2): square waveguide array with axial coupling c1 and diagonal coupling c2; Kerr term is omitted in the low-power regime.
PDF p.3, Eq. (5) and Fig. 3: linear simulations compare Gaussian launch at (kxd,kyd)=(0,0),(pi/2,0),(pi/2,pi/2).
PDF p.4, first paragraph: asymmetry along the zero-quadratic-diffraction direction is attributed to residual third-order diffraction.
records.comparison: Direct prior two-dimensional one-axis versus two-axis pi/2 comparison. Our nearest-neighbor cosine sum is the c2=0 separable limit, not identical to the reported c2=0.043 mm^-1 numerical example.
records.own_inference_from_equation: At the double pi/2 point, Eq. (2) gives diagonal second derivatives zero but mixed derivative d^2 kz/(dkx dky)=4 c2 d^2. For nonzero c2 the Hessian determinant is negative. Therefore this paper must not be cited as demonstrating zero Gaussian curvature at that point.

records.title: Discrete diffraction and shape-invariant beams in optical waveguide arrays
records.read_scope: Introduction, Sec. II.B-D, relevant nearest-neighbor example, conclusion and references; not a claim of detailed review of all 14 pages.
located_evidence: PDF p.3, Eqs. (17)-(19): variance evolves as initial variance plus position-velocity covariance times z plus velocity variance times z^2.
PDF pp.3-4, Sec. II.C and Eqs. (20)-(24): nearest-neighbor band H0=-2 Delta cos p, self-collimation at p=+-pi/2; finite-width spreading is reduced, not eliminated.
PDF pp.5-6, Sec. II.D, Eqs. (30)-(33): coalescing stationary points at self-collimation directions give an amplitude decay scaling z^(-1/3), distinct from the global RMS width.
records.comparison: Strong direct theoretical precedent for our reduced spreading and later deformation. The paper explicitly distinguishes finite-time subdiffraction from a changed long-time RMS growth law.
records.scope_limit: Its statements about finite-moment localization are applied here only to the nonflat cosine band. The discrete Bessel family preserves a functional form with changing parameters, not necessarily rigidly translating Gaussian density.

records.title: Diffraction Management
records.read_scope: Official PRL abstract and metadata; the author's 2002 PhD thesis provides full-text exposition and related experimental discussion. The original four-page PRL PDF was not accessed.
located_evidence: Official abstract: waveguide arrays with reduced, canceled and reversed diffraction were fabricated and experimentally compared with coupled-mode theory.
Author thesis PDF pp.10-12 (printed pp.5-7), Eq. (1.7) and following list: cosine band and zero curvature at |kx|=pi/(2d).

Author thesis PDF pp.42-46 (printed pp.37-41), Sec.3.3 and Figs.3.6-3.7: fixed pi/2 tilt retains higher-order asymmetric spreading; alternating opposite tilts in zigzag arrays cancel higher orders within coupled-mode theory.
records.comparison: Foundational experimental precedent for diffraction management. Uniform inflection-point propagation and longitudinally alternating zigzag cancellation are distinct; only the former matches the present static lattice.

records.title: Anomalous Refraction and Diffraction in Discrete Optical Systems
records.read_scope: Official APS abstract and metadata; full text not obtained in this branch.
located_evidence: Official abstract reports experimental control of diffraction magnitude and sign by launch conditions, including arrested spreading.
Longhi 2009 Sec. II.C identifies this article as the experimental Gaussian self-collimation example.
records.comparison: Supporting experimental history; do not attribute uninspected quantitative details to this paper.

additional_leads_not_promoted_to_core_ev.reason: Author institution verifies metadata and abstract; full text not assessed. Its nonlinear elliptic solitons are not direct evidence for our linear packet.

additional_leads_not_promoted_to_core_ev.reason: Curved, longitudinally engineered arrays; distinct mechanism from uniform static nearest-neighbor propagation.

The local Python environment lacks requests; downloads succeeded using standard-library urllib without installing packages.
ResearchGate snippets were used for discovery only; Chen scientific assessment uses the author-group host.
No subscription access, citation-count ranking, Scopus/Web of Science exhaustive search, or formal PRISMA claim.

Stopped after finding direct two-dimensional launch comparisons, nearest-neighbor pi/2 theory and foundational experimental records; further broad hits mostly concerned different modulated or nonlinear systems.
